title: When is the deepest drawdown also the longest?
abstract: arXiv:2610.41990v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Does the deepest drawdown take the longest to recover? For random walks with iid increments of positive finite mean, we find that the deepest and longest episodes are eventually distinct almost surely under light-tailed losses, but coincide with probability tending to one under heavy-tailed losses. More precisely, when losses have a finite exponential moment, the deepest episode's duration, relative to the longest among $n$ episodes, converges in probability to an explicit $\rho\in(0,1)$, while its descending duration rank is $n^{1-\rho+o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)}$. These limits hold for every fixed number of leading depths; in the Gaussian model, $\rho=1/2$, independently of drift and variance. The separation reflects the different exponential costs of reaching a large depth and sustaining a long episode. translated_title: 最深的回撤何时也是最长的回撤？
translated_abstract: 最深的回撤是否需要最长的时间来恢复？对于具有独立同分布增量且均值为正且有限的随机游走，我们发现：在轻尾损失下，最深与最长的回撤区间最终几乎必然不同；而在重尾损失下，两者重合的概率趋于1。更精确地说，当损失具有有限指数矩时，最深回撤区间的持续时间相对于 n 个区间中最长者，依概率收敛到一个显式常数 ρ∈(0,1)，而其按持续时间降序排列的排名为 n^(1-ρ+o_P(1))。这些极限对所有固定数目的最深区间均成立；在高斯模型中，ρ=1/2，与漂移和方差无关。这种分离反映了“达到较大深度”与“维持长时间区间”所需指数代价的不同。对于正则变化的重尾损失，一次共同的大损失同时主导深度与持续时间：持续时间之比几乎必然趋于1，而对于（后文截断）……
tldr: 该研究揭示了回撤深度与持续时间的渐近关系：对均值为正的独立同分布增量随机游走，轻尾损失下最深与最长回撤区间几乎必然分离（最深回撤的相对时长收敛于显式常数ρ，高斯模型中为1/2），而重尾损失下一次大损失同时主导深度与时长，使两者重合的概率趋于1。
en_tdlr: For random walks with iid positive-mean increments, the deepest and longest drawdowns are asymptotically distinct almost surely under light-tailed losses (with the deepest episode's duration ratio converging to an explicit constant ρ, e.g. 1/2 in the Gaussian case), but coincide with probability tending to one under heavy-tailed losses, where a single large loss governs both depth and duration.
